Title: Effects of a leaflet on breast cancer screening knowledge, explicit attitudes, and implicit associations
Author: Kregting et al.
Comment: The paper reports ranges, not SDs, for follow-up knowledge. No SD, SE, confidence interval, exact p-value, degrees of freedom, or test statistic is reported, so SDs and Hedges’ g cannot validly be derived from the supplied text. The reported p-value is only the inequality p < 0.001 and is therefore not entered as an exact numeric p-value. Group Ns are the final analyzed questionnaire-completer counts reported for the two conditions; the knowledge row does not separately state outcome-specific Ns. M_diff is computed per the extraction convention as group 2 minus group 1: 9.6 − 9.9 = −0.3; because group 1 is the intervention, the raw intervention-minus-control difference is +0.3 points.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Leaflet condition') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type

Title: Effect of information about the benefits and harms of mammography on women’s decision making: The InforMa randomised controlled trial
Author: Pérez-Lacasta et al.
Comment: The paper reports no group-specific SDs or SEs for this knowledge outcome. SDs were derived using the synthesis-plan approximation SD ≈ sqrt(n) × (CI width/3.92), where CI width = 6.44 − 4.5 = 1.94. Because this is a cluster-randomized trial, effective sample sizes were used: 400 analyzed women across 40 randomized BHAs gives average cluster size 10; using the paper’s stated ICC assumption of 0.1 gives design effect 1 + (10 − 1)×0.1 = 1.9, hence effective n = 203/1.9 and 197/1.9. Derived SDs are therefore approximately 5.115 and 5.039. SE_diff was derived from the reported 95% CI as (6.44 − 4.5)/3.92 = 0.4949. The ICC of 0.1 was a sample-size-planning assumption, not an observed outcome-specific ICC; sensitivity analysis is required. The reported p-value is “< 0.001”; 0.001 is stored only as the reported upper bound, not as an exact value.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention: decision-aid leaflet with detailed information on benefits and harms') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: Breast cancer screening decision support and informed choice

Medium: Mailed leaflet followed by web or telephone questionnaire

Recruitment source: Random samples of women from 40 Basic Health Areas participating in four Spanish public breast cancer screening programs
Outcome measurement: Number of marks obtained across conceptual and numerical knowledge questions about mortality benefit, false-positive screening results, and overdiagnosis

Title: Use of a decision aid including information on overdetection to support informed choice about breast cancer screening: a randomised controlled trial
Author: Hersch et al.
Comment: The paper does not report group SDs for this outcome. Following the synthesis contract’s specified equal-group approximation, each SD was derived as sqrt(419) × (2.21−1.11) / 3.92 = 5.74; these SDs are imputed/derived and should be sensitivity-tested. M_diff was computed using the required field convention group 2 minus group 1: 11.84−13.49 = −1.65. The paper itself reports the opposite-direction intervention-minus-control difference as 1.66 (95% CI 1.11 to 2.21); the 0.01 discrepancy reflects subtraction of rounded displayed means. The p value is reported as p<0.0001, so the stored numeric value 0.0001 is an upper bound rather than an exact p value.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention decision aid including overdetection information') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
